title: Load semantic artifacts through a local API
summary: Add a dependency-free Node server that reads the manifest-indexed artifact graph and exposes review data and explicit errors.
rationale: A server-side reader provides deterministic file access now and leaves room for Git-backed endpoints later without coupling the POC to browser file APIs.

decisions.summary: Use only Node built-in modules for the POC server and tests.
decisions.rationale: The experiment should test the artifact workflow rather than framework setup or dependency choices.

decisions.summary: Resolve requirements and stages exclusively from manifest IDs.
decisions.rationale: This follows the standard and makes missing or mismatched documents explicit instead of silently discovering files.

decisions.summary: Expose the single schema-validated working stage separately from canonical stages.
decisions.rationale: The POC must be able to inspect artifacts while it is being implemented, before the current stage has a commit hash.

alternatives.approach: Build a static browser-only app using the File System Access API.
alternatives.reasonRejected: The POC needs predictable local file access and later Git diff execution, which are simpler behind a narrow local server.

risks.summary: The POC reader currently checks graph consistency but does not execute the canonical JSON Schemas.
risks.mitigation: Add schema-backed validation status in a later stage and keep the skill CLI as the authoritative writer validation.

validation.summary: Covers loading the live working artifact, explicit missing-document errors, and the HTTP review endpoint.
